items.title: George Mitchell Interview, 1959-07-01
items.q: Simeon was the only one I can remember on the clarinet... Yeah, Simeon was very good.

ctx.x: Yeah, yeah. And in fact, he'd, he'd have the parts for all the guys to play. For all of them. Yeah, yeah. Uh, and, uh, uh, you take that, uh, Simeon, he was another guy, he could, get, uh, get the idea of what, and then he could, and then he would, uh, and then he would, uh, he would, uh, he would tell him, just throw, throw the music away, you know. Play, play. And then he would give him ideas something about what to play. You know, how to, if you did, uh, a little slow on that.

Would he show you on the piano? Something? Yeah. Yeah. Give you an idea about what. When you first took up a new piece, I'd say that Black Belt and Stomp, or Dr. Jazz, or, or Jelly Roll Blues, would he play it all the way through for you first on the piano to show you how it goes? Or what would he do?
